full_judgment: 13. We find from the record that included in the exhibits was the decree in Other Class Suit No. 211 of 1982, marked as Ext. 5. That suit was filed with a view to seeking release of the suit land from the vested property list. In that suit Nagendra Nath Nandi was substituted by his two sons, namely Pritish Kumar Nandi and Tapan Kumar Nandi as plaintiff Nos. 7 and 8 as his heirs. We are not aware whether that decree came under challenge subsequently. However, it is apparent from that decree that Nagendra Nath Nandi left behind 2 sons as heirs, namely Pritish and Tapan. The decree being part of the record and having been exhibited in the instant suit, we cannot but hold that the plaintiffs purchased their land from the only heirs of Nagendra Nath Nandi. Moreover, the title deed of the plaintiffs having not been challenged, the presumption is in favour of the plaintiffs as to title of the suit land. As stated earlier, the trial Court found possession in favour of the plaintiffs and that finding was not reversed by the appellate Court.
